evidence.notes: Initial auto-upgrade picked FOODON:00004411 (dry cow / non-lactating cow), which is the WRONG sense. Manure-as-ingredient is properly modeled in ENVO. ENVO:00003031 (animal manure) is the closest broad match available; cow-specific manure is not in ENVO.

Minted kgmicrobe.ingredient:dry_cow-manure and anchored to ENVO:00003031 'animal manure' as a narrowMatch (#391). The record previously HELD ENVO:00003031 as its identifier while grading the mapping BROAD_MATCH — in MIM the identifier IS the ontology CURIE, so it asserted identity with animal manure and simultaneously graded that it was not that. §3 step 3 gives a record narrower than every available term its own identity and anchors it to the parent asymmetrically, which is what this does. Step 1 was checked first: 'cow manure' returns no term in ENVO, AGRO or FOODON, and ENVO:01001116 'bovine dairy liquid manure' is LIQUID, the opposite of this record. The predicate follows the corpus convention used by all 141 other asymmetric rows rather than the SKOS-literal direction; that discrepancy is #390 and cannot be changed here without inverting those rows downstream.
